question.text: For a Category III AIF dealing in listed equities and exchange-traded derivatives, Mark-to-Market valuation is crucial PRIMARILY because:

answer.text: It permits the manager to smooth NAV volatility by averaging prices across the week
It converts cash profits into notional profits for tax deferral
SEBI mandates MTM only for commodity futures, not equity futures
It ensures the NAV reflects current fair market value, enables fair Incentive Fee computation, and provides a fair redemption price to exiting unitholders

explanation.text: The Logic: Mark-to-Market revises NAV to represent the true worth of the portfolio on each valuation day. It supports fair incentive-fee computation based on actual market returns, fair redemption/withdrawal pricing for unitholders, and accurate reconciliation of derivative positions. The Trap: Option A describes price-smoothing, which is the opposite of MTM and would distort NAV. Option B is incorrect — MTM has no tax-deferral effect on the fund. Option C invents a selective SEBI mandate that does not exist. Note: MTM is integral to investor protection in Cat III AIFs because incentive fees and redemption prices are calculated off NAV — distorted NAV directly transfers wealth between investors and the manager.
